title: Can the figure alone show which angle is greater?
description: Two angles at the vertex O point in different directions. Looking at them does not settle which is greater, so one is traced and laid over the other with the vertices together. The reverse test, with the other angle traced, is the check.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two angles point in different directions, lay one over the other, or measure, to decide. Watch for students who give an answer from the figure alone.

video_script.why: The child sees that looking at the figure is not enough and decides by laying one angle over the other.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure of the angles XOY and AOB with the vertex O
video_script.anchor: the figure of the book with the angles XOY and AOB pointing in different directions
video_script.payoff_line: From the figure alone we cannot say, so we lay one angle over the other

final_answer.value: from the figure we cannot say; superimposition or measurement is necessary
final_answer.spoken: from the figure alone we cannot say, so we lay one angle over the other, or measure them

maths_rules: figure: vertex O; angle XOY and angle AOB point in different directions
by looking at the figure we cannot say which is greater
trace angle AOB, lay it on angle XOY with the vertices together and one arm along one arm
if the other arm falls inside, AOB is smaller; if outside, AOB is larger; if on the arm, they are equal
check: trace XOY and lay it on AOB, which must give the matching result
video_script.design: One idea: decide by superimposition or measurement, never by the eye alone. One figure stays on the board.
open_questions: The worklist says the angles look close in size; the book's figure could not be viewed, so the video says only that they point in different directions.
